item.title: Expensive Models vs. Cheap Models
item.description:
The Old Wisdom

There used to be a prevailing view: “Always use the most expensive model.” Anthropic’s Opus, for example.

The reasoning was straightforward: the most expensive model is the smartest model.

For any given task, the most expensive model gets it right in one shot. A cheaper model might get it wrong, and after a few rounds of correction, you’ve spent more in time and tokens than if you’d just used the expensive one from the start.

item.title: Expensive vs Cheap Models
item.description:
The Old Wisdom

There’s a conventional argument that goes: “Always use the most expensive model.”

The logic is straightforward — the most expensive model is also the smartest one. For any given task, the top-tier model gets it right in one shot. A cheaper model? It might fumble, need corrections, and by the time you’ve iterated, you’ve burned through more tokens and time than if you’d just picked the expensive model to begin with.
